conviction_note: Two-thirds of Q3 revenue is public (Jul $825.8M + Aug $812.1M) and September tracks +15-17% on Baird's FDI note, so revenue lands near the Zacks $2.49B bar and EPS near $0.34. The print turns on gross margin, where a record Q3 diesel spike (CFO: fuel sits in GM and was 'still a headwind') pulls against a narrowing contract/non-contract mix gap and falling headcount. Findings roughly offset (sum -0.1). The scaled number leans slightly negative (p_up 46) because the name sold its last three prints on GM, the 25d skew is +6.4 vol points with put/call OI 2.13, and the stock sits 2.8% off its 52-week high, above the ~$49.50 average target. abs_move 5.0 is a little under the 5.67% option-implied move and well above the 2.78% median reaction.
bar: Revenue: Zacks consensus $2.49B (+16.6% y/y), EPS $0.34 (Yahoo/Zacks, 2026-10-13, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/heres-must-know-ahead-fastenals-131200740.html). MarketBeat has $2.4369B / $0.3379 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-fastenal-fast-set-to-post-earnings-on-wednesday-2026-10-07/), which looks stale from before August's sales. The revenue bar is DISPUTED ($2.437B vs $2.49B), so every revenue-dependent finding is capped small. The EPS bar agrees at ~$0.34. My tracking estimate: Jul $825.8M + Aug $812.1M = $1,637.9M. September 2025 implied $721.6M over 21 days ($34.36M a day: Q3'25 $2,133.3M less Jul'25 $715.0M and Aug'25 $696.7M). September 2026 also has 21 days. At Sept +15.3% (Baird) Q3 is $2.470B; at +16.8% (FAST's seasonal benchmark per Baird) it is $2.481B. Midpoint ~$2.476B, or -0.6% to -0.4% against Zacks and +1.6% against MarketBeat. Gross margin: no consensus found. The company gives no GM guide; the Q2 call said the normal Q2-to-Q3 seasonal decline is 10-20bp off Q2's 44.6% (Q3'25 was 45.3%).
positioning_check: Short interest 3.12% of float, days to cover 5.78, up 2.9% m/m (MarketBeat, 2026-08-12, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/fastenal-nasdaqfast-sets-new-1-year-high-heres-why-2026-08-12/). Sweep row: Benzinga 3.6% of float rising; Equibles 4.1 DTC, undated. Not a crowded short. No September settlement found. Options from the baseline: 25d skew +6.41 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 2.13, event-implied move 5.67% against a 2.78% median of 7 prior reactions, 20d realised vol 16.2%. Tape: +3.06% over 20 days, 2.79% under the 52-week high. Sell side: Wolfe initiated Underperform with a $51 target on 2026-09-15; the average target is $49.50 against a $50.92 spot (MarketBeat 2026-10-07).

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is two-thirds public and tracks ~$2.47-2.48B: July daily sales $37.54M (+15.5%, 22 days, $825.8M) and August $38.67M (+16.6%, 21 days, $812.1M) from Fastenal's own monthly releases. Matching Zacks's $2.49B needs September daily sales of ~+17-18% y/y; Baird models +15.3% and says FAST's own seasonal benchmark implies ~+16.8%. So revenue is in line to fractionally light against Zacks and a clear beat against the stale MarketBeat $2.437B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sales beats have not been paid lately. Q2 2026 (2026-07-14): revenue $2.39B beat $2.34B with EPS in line and GM down 75bp, and the stock fell 2.78%. 2026-04-13: -6.85%. 2026-01-20: -2.56% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the monthly numbers are public. The open part is September plus the dispersion between estimate providers ($2.437B vs $2.49B). If the market held the stale lower bar, the stock would have run harder after the August print; instead it is +3% over 20 days.
findings.independence: July release via search summary (https://s23.q4cdn.com/591718779/files/doc_financials/2026/Q2/07-2026-sales-numbers-v4.pdf, 2026-08-06) and Q3 2025 base (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251010013138/en/Fastenal-Company-Reports-2025-Third-Quarter-Earnings). The September estimate shares the Baird FDI document with the next finding.

findings.finding: The Baird/FCH Fastener Distributor Index for September 2026 (published 2026-10-06) jumped to 66.6 from 58.3, the highest since July 2018. The sales sub-index hit a record 91.5 (77.8 unadjusted, vs 65.5 in August). The Forward-Looking Indicator is 63.6, the best since March 2022, and 44% of respondents expect higher activity in six months against 7% lower. Respondents cite record September and Q3 sales and data-center demand. This points to a strong September exit and a constructive Q4/October tone on the call, above the +15.3% Baird itself conservatively models.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Demand and sales strength (13-14 straight double-digit months) has not stopped three consecutive negative reactions; the stock trades on GM rather than sales (baseline: -2.56, -6.85, -2.78).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the FDI is public and Baird published it. Baird's own September model (+15.3%) sits ~150bp below FAST's benchmark 'as conservatism', so the street's September number may lag the survey. If priced, Zacks would sit well above $2.49B and the skew would not be bid to the downside.
findings.independence: ISM Manufacturing PMI was 54.5 for September 2026, its ninth month of expansion, with new orders 55.3 (https://www.miningstockeducation.com/2026/10/manufacturing-pmi-at-54-5-september-2026-ism-manufacturing-pmi-report/). It is a proxy, but a broad one. Grainger guided Q3 daily organic growth above 12% (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/grainger-beats-q2-earnings-estimates-margin-gains-raises-outlook).

findings.finding: U.S. on-highway diesel spiked through Q3 2026: about $4.57/gal in early July, $5.31 by late July, $5.97 in the week of 7 September and above $6 (a series record) by mid-September. That is a materially higher quarterly average than Q2. On the Q2 call the CFO said fuel was 'still a headwind' and that incrementals could improve if fuel declined in H2; Florness said most diesel cost sits in gross margin. The 10-Q already cited fuel inflation in transportation costs as a Q2 GM headwind. This points to GM below the normal 10-20bp seasonal step-down from 44.6% (Q3'25: 45.3%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GM is the line this stock trades on. Q2 2026: GM -75bp y/y, stock -2.78% despite a revenue beat (https://www.sahmcapital.com/news/content/why-is-fastenal-stock-trading-lower-today-2026-07-14). Q1 2026: GM -50bp, stock -6.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: diesel at a record is public and agrees with the downside skew. What is unpriced is the size in Fastenal's GM, which the company does not quantify, and the fact that management's stated hope of H2 fuel relief went the other way. If fully priced, the stock would not sit 2.8% off its 52-week high.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15267023071093760) confirms the channel (fuel in GM, a headwind). Work Truck Online for the late-July $5.31 (https://www.worktruckonline.com/news/july-diesel-trends-update-v2). The magnitude is macro-to-company transmission, i.e. a proxy.

findings.finding: The customer-mix headwind to GM is narrowing. In Q2 2026 contract daily sales grew 17.6% against 7.3% for non-contract, a 10.3-point gap; in August 2026 it was 19.0% against 11.0%, an 8-point gap. Non-contract (smaller, higher-margin customers) is accelerating, and the share of in-market locations growing rose to 67.2% from 62.5% a year earlier. That shrinks the large-account mix dilution management cited as a Q2 GM drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Mix has been the recurring explanation for GM compression, and GM compression drew the last three negative reactions; no print has yet shown mix turning favourable.
findings.why_not_priced: It is buried in a line of the monthly PDF that wire copy does not carry; previews talk about headline daily sales. If priced, GM previews would point to stabilisation, and the skew would not be paying for downside.
findings.independence: The Q2 contract and non-contract figures come from the Q2 release (https://s23.q4cdn.com/591718779/files/doc_financials/2026/Q2/EX_99-1-06-30-2026-Earnings-Release-Final-no-Footers.pdf). This shares the August PDF with findings 1 and 5.

findings.finding: Headcount is falling while sales accelerate. Total FTE was 21,989 at end-August, down 1.0% from July's 22,206 and below ~22,230 at Q2-end. Selling FTE was 15,514, -0.5% y/y, against +16.6% sales. With ~70% of SG&A people-related, this supports SG&A leverage beyond Q2's 23.5% of sales and offsets part of any GM shortfall at the operating line. Rough model: Q3 op margin ~21% and EPS ~$0.34-0.35 against $0.34.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 delivered SG&A leverage (23.5% vs 24.4%), yet incrementals of ~low-20s with bonuses higher still drew -2.78%; leverage has not been rewarded when GM fell.
findings.why_not_priced: The headcount table sits at the bottom of the monthly PDF. Zacks EPS has been unchanged at $0.34 for 60 days with ESP -0.97%, so estimates have not been lifted for leverage.
findings.independence: Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15267023071093760): Florness said the company can grow ~15% on low-single-digit headcount growth, and bonuses ran ~45% higher q/q. Bonuses are a counter-pressure, already netted in the size. This shares the August PDF with findings 1 and 4.

findings.finding: Positioning and sell-side stance into the print. The stock is $50.92, 2.8% under its 52-week high and above the $49.50 average target (6 Buy / 5 Hold / 2 Sell). Wolfe initiated Underperform ($51) on 2026-09-15. Directors sold shares in July and August (Heise sold 63.6% of her stake, $1.75M, on 2026-08-05). The name has fallen after each of its last three prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Three straight negative reactions (-2.56, -6.85, -2.78) after a run of four positive ones in 2025 (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it agrees with the +6.4 skew and P/C OI 2.13. What it adds is that the stock trades above the average target with no crowded short to squeeze (3.1% of float), so there is room for a 'good but not good enough' sell. If priced out, the stock would be near the target rather than above it.
findings.independence: The baseline options block (skew +6.41, P/C OI 2.13) and short interest of 3.12% / 5.78 DTC (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/fastenal-nasdaqfast-sets-new-1-year-high-heres-why-2026-08-12/).

findings.finding: Input-cost inflation re-accelerated in Q3. The ISM September prices index jumped 6.8 points to 77.9. In the FDI, 85% of fastener distributors report higher y/y pricing, and the m/m pricing index was 77.6 in August and 64.8 in September. Fastenal's net price/cost was -40bp in Q2, and the CFO declined to predict neutrality before Q4. Rapid supplier inflation tends to widen the price/cost lag before pricing catches up, though it also lifts reported revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Price/cost was the main named driver of the Q2 GM decline (-40bp) that drew -2.78%.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro series are public; how they hit Fastenal's price/cost is unquantified by the company. This is a proxy, sized small.
findings.independence: The FDI September pricing data (https://www.nfda-fastener.org/assets/docs/FDI_Report_September_2026.pdf) and MSC's Q3 call naming tungsten inflation and further price actions (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/01/msc-industrial-msm-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Distinct from the diesel finding: product cost, not freight.

findings.finding: Possible small IEEPA tariff refund in Q3. The Q2 10-Q says Fastenal filed IEEPA refund claims in Q2 on entries where it was importer of record and booked no receivable at June 30, but 'may recognize additional benefits in future periods'. It also says direct exposure is limited because it is not importer of record for most products.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance at Fastenal. Grainger lapped a Q2 tariff-refund benefit and guided Q3 margin lower because of it.
findings.why_not_priced: Not in any estimate, but the company itself calls it limited. It is a one-off with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction.

baseline_tension: The negative findings (diesel, price/cost, positioning) agree with the +6.4 put skew and are likely partly priced. The positives (record FDI, narrowing mix gap, headcount leverage) cut against the skew but land on lines this stock has not paid for in three prints, so the net is near zero and p_up sits only slightly below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (this name sold its last three prints): FDI demand finding cut from +0.8 to +0.5; mix and headcount positives each cut from +0.4 to +0.3.
Rule 6 (disputed bar, $2.437B vs $2.49B): revenue finding left capped at +0.2; the EPS bar agrees at $0.34 and is stated in `bar`.

Rule 5 and rule 7 (a proxy, agreeing with the skew): diesel finding cut from -1.0 to -0.7; positioning finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6. Short interest was checked: 3.1% of float, not crowded, so there was no squeeze discount.
Rule 2: the IEEPA refund stays a one-off at +0.1. The sum is unchanged at -0.1; abs_move and p_up are unchanged.
